newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq hopes for trade deals at fair.
newsitem.headline: Iraq hopes for trade deals at fair.

text.p: Iraq said on Thursday it hoped to sign trade deals at a business fair in Baghdad next month even though these depended on a stalled oil-for-food agreement with the United Nations.
Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saled said 16 countries and 45 multinational companies would attend the trade fair in Baghdad from November 1 for 15 days.

"So far 16 countries have announced their participation in the fair, twice the number last year," Saleh told a news conference. Among these countries were China, Turkey, South Korea, Greece, Jordan, Algeria, Yemen, Tunisia and others.

"Forty-five companies are attending -- an increase of two and half fold on last year's participation," Saleh said, adding that French, Chinese, Russian, Indian, Turkish and Egyptian firms and others from the former Soviet bloc were attending.
The minister said Iraq was ready to conclude trade deals with these companies under an "oil-for-food" deal Iraq signed with the United Nations on May 20.

The deal, stalled over security reasons in Iraq's north caused by fighting between Kurdish factions with Iraq's participation initially, allows Baghdad oil sales worth $2 billion every six months to buy food and medicine. The Iraqi population has suffered under tough U.N. sanctions sor six years imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

"Yes, the Ministry of Trade and other ministries are ready to sign contracts with these companies and countries...based on the oil-for-food and medicine agreement with the United Nations," Saleh said.
Saleh said Iraq's trade with Jordan would continue. "Our trade with Jordan is continuing unabated," he said.
Trade between Baghdad and Amman reached its lowest ebb last year when Jordan provided refuge to two senior Iraqi defectors, killed in Baghdad soon after their return home last February.
Jordan's King Hussein has distanced himself from Iraq, mending ties with both Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, diehard enemies of Baghdad.
Iraq supplies Jordan with oil. Under a deal signed last year, Baghdad is to supply Amman with 4.4 million tonnes of crude and byproducts in 1996.
"We have no amendment to our trade dealing with Jordan," Saleh said.
Saleh lauded Iraq's trade relations with Egypt saying that 25 Egyptian firms would attend the fair.
"Trade relations with Egypt are continuing...We buy rice from Egyptian companies," he said.
